world_money_map.summary: Restrictive policy is coexisting with selective rather than uniform risk aversion. The Fed and BOJ have tightened, but live controls show that already-priced action signs are weaker price drivers than expectation-adjusted future paths, relative rates, energy inflation and positioning. The Sep. 15 U.S. tax/Treasury-settlement event caused a large TGA rebuild and reserve drain, yet repo median/tails stayed orderly and official Standing Repo take-up was only $102M that day. This materially falsifies a deterministic 'sub-10%-of-GDP Fed liquidity -> immediate funding stress' rule. Capital allocation is cross-sectional: broad U.S. equity funds are losing capital while selected sectors, Asian equities, government/short-duration bonds and precious metals receive flows; BTC ETF demand improved for one completed session but has not yet become a durable accumulation regime.
world_money_map.regime: RESTRICTIVE POLICY / SELECTIVE CAPITAL ALLOCATION / EXPECTATION-SENSITIVE PRICING
world_money_map.liquidity: RESERVE DRAIN REALIZED WITHOUT BINDING BROAD REPO SCARCITY; AGGREGATE FED LIQUIDITY IS A SENSITIVITY STATE, NOT A TRIGGER
world_money_map.credit: NO VALIDATED BROAD FUNDING OR CREDIT CRISIS
world_money_map.policy: FED AND BOJ TIGHTER; MARKET RESPONSE DEPENDS ON PRICED PATH VERSUS REALIZED PATH/GUIDANCE

money_flows.title: Broad U.S. equity redemptions with sector/region rotation
money_flows.direction: BROAD US EQUITY FUNDS -> SELECTIVE SECTORS / ASIA / OTHER ASSET BUCKETS
money_flows.confidence: HIGH on observed flows; MODERATE on source-destination matching
money_flows.summary: Reuters reported $31.44B of U.S. equity-fund outflows for a fourth consecutive week. U.S. sector funds still received about $2.29B. A broader global dataset showed $23.21B global equity outflow, $6.26B Asian equity inflow and $4.49B sector-fund inflow led by technology, financials and consumer discretionary.

money_flows.title: Government/short-duration demand remains relatively resilient
money_flows.summary: Short/intermediate government and Treasury funds received stronger inflows while aggregate bond flows were weak and some higher-risk credit buckets lost capital, consistent with demand for yield with less credit/duration risk.

money_flows.title: Commodity fund flow favors precious metals over energy
money_flows.direction: COMMODITY FUND CAPITAL -> GOLD / PRECIOUS METALS
money_flows.summary: Global commodity funds received about $1.17B in the latest weekly data, concentrated in gold/precious metals, while energy funds had about $148M of outflows.

money_flows.title: BTC ETF demand improved but has not established accumulation
money_flows.direction: MARGINAL BTC ETF DEMAND IMPROVED; DURABILITY UNCONFIRMED
money_flows.confidence: HIGH on completed data; LOW-MODERATE on persistence
money_flows.summary: Farside records +$159.5M U.S. spot BTC ETF net flow on Sep. 17 after -$450.4M Sep. 15 and -$295.9M Sep. 16. The three completed sessions remain net negative; Sep. 17 was concentrated in IBIT. ETH remained -$39.3M on Sep. 17. Sep. 18 was unfinalized at cutoff.

money_flows.title: Treasury cash drain did not become broad funding stress
money_flows.direction: PRIVATE/BANK CASH -> TREASURY; RESERVES DOWN; REPO STRESS NOT OBSERVED
money_flows.summary: Fed H.4.1 shows Sep. 16 Wednesday TGA +$148.003B week/week and reserve balances -$114.971B. On Sep. 15 SOFR median was 3.64%, SOFR 99th percentile 3.72% and TGCR 99th percentile 3.65%, only modestly above the prior day. Primary NY Fed repo-operation data show zero morning Standing Repo take-up and only $102M accepted in the afternoon on Sep. 15, followed by zero morning and $254M afternoon on Sep. 16. These are trivial relative to the reserve swing and strongly argue against generalized scarcity.
money_flows.source: Federal Reserve H.4.1; New York Fed reference rates and repo-operation API

opportunities.title: Broad macro one-factor trade
opportunities.thesis: Simple rules such as 'hike = currency up/risk down' and 'reserve drain = funding stress' have failed recent live controls. Oil, long yields, relative policy paths, growth/inflation information and positioning conflict. No broad directional edge clears the evidence bar.
opportunities.invalidation: A cross-asset regime emerges with independent flow, rates, credit and price confirmation.

opportunities.title: AI/technology physical-investment chain
opportunities.confidence: MODERATE structural; LOW asset-level until valuation work is complete
opportunities.thesis: Sector flows and prior capex/financing evidence remain consistent with capital moving through semiconductors, data centers, networking, power/grid and cooling. No individual-asset BUY is promoted without valuation and cash-flow capture evidence.
opportunities.invalidation: Capex commitments fall materially, financing tightens, monetization/utilization disappoints or valuation implies unattractive forward returns.

opportunities.title: Tokenized-securities infrastructure
opportunities.thesis: The SEC's Sep. 17 temporary conditional innovation exemption removes a specific regulatory barrier for tokenized NMS stock venues. Value capture must be mapped at venue, custody, settlement and liquidity layers rather than assumed to accrue to generic crypto tokens.
opportunities.invalidation: Low adoption, weak liquidity, adverse final rulemaking/legal challenge or economics accruing elsewhere.

opportunities.title: BTC after Sep. 18 rebound
opportunities.thesis: BTC recovered to roughly $80k-$81k and Sep. 17 ETF flow turned positive, but the preceding two-day outflow cluster is larger, Sep. 18 ETF data were not final, ETH remains weaker and venue-grade derivatives/exchange-flow decomposition is incomplete. Short covering is plausible but not yet primary-source validated.
confirmations: Several completed positive ETF sessions with breadth
BTC relative strength versus comparable risk assets
Venue-grade OI/funding/liquidations without excessive fresh leverage
opportunities.invalidation: Large ETF redemptions resume, rebound fails, or leverage rises sharply without spot breadth.

risks.title: Energy/rates can re-tighten financial conditions
risks.summary: Oil remains above $100 and the Fed is tighter. A renewed supply shock or further hawkish path repricing can lift long yields and required returns.
risks.invalidation: Energy scarcity eases and long/real yields decline without a growth shock.

risks.title: JPY intervention risk
risks.summary: USD/JPY rose toward 158 despite the BOJ hike because the hike was expected and guidance/dissents implied a shallower follow-on path. Japanese authorities signaled concern, making post-move chasing unattractive.
risks.invalidation: Authorities tolerate sustained weakness and relative-rate spreads keep widening without intervention action/rhetoric.

risks.title: Middle-East energy logistics remain fat-tailed
risks.confidence: HIGH tail-risk existence; LOW directional confidence
risks.summary: Benchmark crude eased as rerouting and inventories improved effective supply, but route damage and product bottlenecks remain. Fresh attacks or loss of substitutes can restore scarcity quickly.
risks.invalidation: Shipping/routes normalize, damaged capacity returns, physical differentials/product cracks normalize and inventories rebuild.

causal_chains.title: TGA rebuild -> reserve drain -> stress only if intermediation binds
causal_chains.summary: Tax/settlement flows -> TGA rises -> reserves fall -> potential repo sensitivity; if private intermediation/backstops retain capacity -> repo median/tails and Standing Repo use remain small -> no generalized funding-stress transmission. Sep. 15-16 is a matched non-crisis control.

causal_chains.title: Expected central-bank action -> relative path/guidance drives repricing
causal_chains.summary: Pre-event pricing embeds the action -> expected action is delivered -> action sign adds little new information -> vote/guidance/future relative path drives FX/rates repricing. BOJ Sep. 18 and FOMC Sep. 16 support this model.

causal_chains.title: Energy disruption -> price depends on effective deliverable supply
causal_chains.summary: Infrastructure shock -> scarcity expectation -> price premium; rerouting, inventory, grade/product compatibility, freight and diplomacy change effective deliverable supply -> benchmark premium can reverse while physical stress persists.

discoveries.title: Aggregate Fed liquidity is a sensitivity state, not a scarcity trigger
discoveries.summary: The Sep. 15-16 drain realized, but repo median/tails stayed calm and Standing Repo take-up was only $102M on Sep. 15 and $254M on Sep. 16 afternoons. Intermediation capacity must actually bind before low aggregate liquidity becomes funding stress.

discoveries.title: Expectation-adjusted policy path is more informative than action sign
discoveries.summary: The widely expected BOJ hike was followed by yen depreciation; the heavily priced FOMC hike also produced offsetting cross-asset reactions. Historical event testing is still required.

discoveries.title: Effective deliverable supply matters more than gross commodity disruption
discoveries.summary: Brent reversed despite continuing infrastructure/geopolitical stress as rerouting, inventories and diplomacy improved effective supply. Local grade/product scarcity can still persist.

discoveries.title: Cross-sectional flow analysis can be more informative than risk-on/risk-off labels
discoveries.summary: Broad U.S./global equity outflows coexist with sector/Asian inflows and precious-metals demand. Persistence and predictive value remain to be tested.

changes_since_previous: The Sep. 15 funding test is now substantially closed: large TGA/reserve movement, calm median/tail repo rates and only $102M Standing Repo use falsify the deterministic scarcity interpretation.
FOMC Sep. 16 and BOJ Sep. 18 provide two live controls favoring expectation-adjusted future-path reasoning over action-sign heuristics.
Broad U.S. equity redemptions are now separated from positive sector/Asian allocations; capital allocation is selective.
BTC ETF flow turned positive Sep. 17 and BTC rebounded above $80k, but the three completed Sep. 15-17 sessions remain net negative and ETH remains weaker; BTC stays WAIT.
Crude research now centers on effective deliverability by route/location/grade/product after substitution and inventories.
unknowns: Sep. 18 BTC/ETH ETF flows were unfinalized at the information cutoff.
Venue-grade BTC derivatives, exchange-flow and options data sufficient to separate spot demand from short covering/fresh leverage have not yet been validated.
The expectation-adjusted policy-surprise model needs a larger timestamp-safe historical sample.
It is unknown whether current sector/region flow dispersion predicts persistent relative returns after rates, earnings and valuation controls.
Middle-East logistics and diplomacy remain nonlinear and can change quickly.
research_frontier: Highest priority: decompose the Sep. 18 BTC rebound with primary/venue-grade open interest, funding, liquidations, exchange/on-chain flows and completed ETF data.
Build timestamp-safe FOMC/BOJ/ECB event study comparing priced action/path with realized action, guidance/vote surprise and 30m/1d/5d market responses.
Build historical tax/Treasury-settlement controls using aggregate liquidity plus dealer/MMF capacity, repo median/tails and official facility use.
Extend energy matched controls to route/location/grade/product deliverability, inventories, freight/insurance and physical differentials.
Test whether broad-equity outflows plus sector-tech inflows predict relative strength after rates, earnings revisions and valuation controls.
Map actual fee/cash-flow capture under the SEC tokenized-securities exemption.
